results.summary: This design scans a 4x4 keypad matrix and displays the pressed key on a 7-segment display. It uses a 16-bit register to store the key state and combinatorial logic to drive the segments. External hardware includes a 4x4 keypad matrix and a 7-segment display. The design lacks debouncing and latching, making it a simple demonstration of keypad interfacing.

This project implements a 4-digit password locker using a 4x4 matrix keypad. It registers a password and then compares subsequent entries, indicating success via an output pin. External hardware includes a keypad, a reset button, and LEDs. The design uses shift registers and state machines to manage password registration and verification.

This is a 32-bit Fibonacci linear feedback shift register with taps at bits 32, 30, 26, and 25. It includes a fail-safe to prevent all-zero lock-up and allows manual initialization via input pins. The design outputs the lower 8 bits and can be tested with a logic analyzer. Silicon testing confirmed it generates a random-looking output.

This is a 32-bit Galois linear feedback shift register with taps at bits 32, 30, 26, and 25. It includes a fail-safe to prevent all-zero lock-up and allows manual initialization via input pins. The design outputs the lower 8 bits and can be tested with a logic analyzer. No silicon test results are provided.

This design implements an 8-bit cyclic redundancy check for error detection in serial data streams. It takes a serial input and provides an 8-bit CRC output. External hardware includes LEDs, a clock source, and switches for reset and input. Silicon testing showed it functioned correctly compared to a software model.

This design implements a 4-bit stochastic multiplier using traditional architecture. It converts two 4-bit binary vectors into stochastic bitstreams using a PRBS and comparator, then multiplies them with an AND gate. External hardware includes an ADLAM2000 for control and analysis. The design is part of a study on stochastic computing.

This is a compact 4-bit stochastic multiplier that uses a Schmitt trigger on input pins as a stochastic resonator. It converts two 4-bit binary vectors into stochastic bitstreams and multiplies them with an AND gate. External hardware includes an ADLAM2000 for control and analysis. The design explores a more compact architecture for stochastic computing.

This is a 2-bit binary calculator that can add, subtract, or multiply two 2-bit numbers. The result is displayed on a 7-segment display. External hardware includes DIP switches for input and a 7-segment display. Silicon testing partially confirmed correct operation for addition and multiplication.

This project is a 1-bit ALU intended as a test tapeout. The documentation is minimal, providing only the title and one-line description. No functional details, pinout, or test information are given. It appears to be a placeholder or experimental design.

This design is a 2-bit synchronous multiplexer with output enable. It selects between two 2-bit inputs based on a select signal and provides both true and complemented outputs, along with parity and population count. The outputs can be tri-stated via an output enable pin. No external hardware is specified, and no silicon test results are provided.
